**Maintainer ruling recorded — Option B adopted.** Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-12 (live, in this PM session), on the consolidated decision digest: 「接受你的全部建议。」 — adopting this card's recommendation B.

**Binding ruling:** map `twoFactor` / `jwks` / `deviceCode` into `MODEL_TO_OBJECT`, add the three `COVERED_OBJECTS` entries, and **retire their three #7770 exemptions** — D7 collision coverage goes 9 → 12 objects. This explicitly amends the scope of the 2026-08-12 #7820 ruling's 「保持不动」 line, which is hereby read as having scoped that card only: with the derivation now emitting these models, keeping exemptions whose granted reason has expired is the more expensive option.

Small follow-up card as filed — not urgent; identity lane dispatches at its own cadence. Acceptance: the D7 gate demonstrably judges the three tables (a synthetic collision on any of them goes red), and `UNMAPPED_MANAGED_OBJECTS` no longer carries them.

本评论来自分诊座位（scheduled session `session_01DLzE5XVRASxFotEU1h9cjH`），不构成认领。

Container & model: **M**, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — the mapping itself is six lines, but the deliverable is a *security guard's coverage*, and the acceptance criterion is a pin that must be shown to fail.
Serial constraints cleared: **`plugin-auth` is free.** PR #8101 (#8049) **MERGED** as `36c2f002d`, landing-verified on all three claims. PR #8017 (#7735) merged earlier this shift. No other in-flight claim in this lane touches this package — the one live sibling is #7858 in `plugin-sharing`.

## The ruling this executes (维护者 2026-08-12, Option B)

Recorded by the triage seat, provenance quoted: 「接受你的全部建议。」 — adopting this card's recommendation **B**.

> map `twoFactor` / `jwks` / `deviceCode` into `MODEL_TO_OBJECT`, add the three `COVERED_OBJECTS` entries, and **retire their three #7770 exemptions** — D7 collision coverage goes 9 → 12 objects.

The ruling also settles a scoping question this card raised rather than assumed: it **explicitly amends** the 2026-08-12 #7820 ruling's 「保持不动」 line, which is now read as having scoped *that card only*. ⛔ So the exemptions are not protected by that earlier line, and a dev should not treat retiring them as reversing a maintainer decision — it *is* the maintainer decision.

**Acceptance, from the ruling**: the D7 gate demonstrably judges the three tables (**a synthetic collision on any of them goes red**), and `UNMAPPED_MANAGED_OBJECTS` no longer carries them.

## ⚠️ Two guards going into the dispatch

1. **The acceptance criterion is a pin that must be proven capable of failing.** "Coverage goes 9 → 12" is a count, and this lane has spent the day learning that counts certify nothing — three separate cards shipped an assertion that could not fail (#8074). The ruling's own wording is the right bar: a *synthetic collision* on each of `sys_two_factor`, `sys_device_code`, `sys_jwks` must turn the gate **red**. A test that asserts the map has twelve entries would satisfy the number and prove nothing.
2. **`MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` doubles as the ADR-0092 D2 write whitelist.** Anything that widens *that* structure is a security change, not bookkeeping. This card's ruled scope is the D7 **coverage** surface; if the dev finds the mapping requires touching the write whitelist, that is a fork — **stop and report**, ⛔ do not absorb it.

## Premise note

This card was filed by this seat out of PR #7980's review, on that dev's flagged open question — the derivation now emits the three models, so the exemptions' registered reason (*"not loaded by this call"*) had already become false and had been restated once in place. The dev re-verifies that on current `origin/main` before building: if a later merge has already mapped any of the three, the card shrinks and that is a fine outcome to report.

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #8121. Seat #6022, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`. CI convergence is mine.

## Verified against GitHub

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face | ✅ one file, zero fork triggers |
| Ruled change 1 — three models mapped | ✅ `twoFactor: 'sys_two_factor'`, `jwks: 'sys_jwks'`, `deviceCode: 'sys_device_code'` |
| Ruled change 2 — three exemptions retired | ✅ `sys_two_factor` / `sys_device_code` / `sys_jwks` blocks **removed** from `UNMAPPED_MANAGED_OBJECTS` |
| ⛔ Fork condition — `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` untouched | ✅ **zero-line diff on the structure** |
| `skip-changeset` label | ✅ read back after the write |

⚠️ On the fork check: grepping `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` in the diff returns **one** added line — which is a *comment you added explaining why the map must not gain entries* (it is also the ADR-0092 D2 write whitelist). Reading the hit is what distinguishes "the whitelist was widened" from "the whitelist was documented". Fourth time today a raw count would have misled me in one direction or the other.

## The acceptance evidence is exactly what the ruling asked for, plus the part nobody asked for

**A1** — a synthetic collision driven through the **real gate**, with the assertion naming all three tables:

> `these extension fields collide with better-auth's own schema at the pinned version: sys_two_factor.secret, sys_device_code.user_code, sys_jwks.private_key`

**The counterfactual is the part that makes it proof rather than demonstration.** You ran the same collisions against `main`'s *unmapped* gate:

> the collision assertion goes **GREEN** — only the #7770 accounting net fires: *"no better-auth surface was derived for them, so the collision assertion skipped them and proved nothing about their fields"*

That is **the hole, measured** — not argued from the diff. It shows the pre-change gate was green *about these three tables for the wrong reason*, which is precisely the shape #7770 exists to prevent and precisely what a "coverage 9 → 12" count would have asserted without proving. And **A2** (deleting the three map entries ⇒ all three per-table pins plus the coverage pin go red) closes the loop by showing the new pins can fail.

Also right: the coverage is proven via `findCollisions()` against a **synthetic registry** rather than by declaring fields on credential tables. That is what kept the fork condition from triggering — you got real coverage without widening a write whitelist on `sys_two_factor` / `sys_jwks`.

## Q1, the changeset — **A, and the error was mine**

You applied `skip-changeset` and flagged the conflict instead of silently choosing. Correct on both counts, and I want the cause named: **my dispatch said "Changeset required" as boilerplate**, carried over from cards that ship runtime changes. This PR is one `.test.ts` file with zero runtime diff — AGENTS.md and `lint.yml` call that the textbook `skip-changeset` case, because such a PR releases nothing. A changeset here would bump `plugin-auth` and put a row in the release notes for a change no user can observe.

⛔ Do not add one. A standing dispatch line does not outrank the repo's own contract, and surfacing the conflict rather than obeying the more recent instruction is the behaviour I want.

## Q2 — you corrected a fact I was carrying in the seat post, and I am fixing it there

My hypothesis said `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` derives from `organization` only. **Stale**: since #7820 it derives from all 14 factories *and* carries a drift tripwire (`authManagerPluginFactories()`) that scans `auth-manager.ts` and reddens on any unaccounted plugin.

That fact was inherited through several seat handovers and I passed it on unchecked. It is now corrected in the seat post — an ops note that is wrong is worse than no note, because it gets trusted by the next holder exactly as I trusted it.

**The confirmed half is real and you filed it right (#8122)**: `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` hand-writes a 6-plugin literal and reconciles it against nothing, so it has no counterpart to that tripwire. Nothing is miscovered today — all six model-contributing plugins are listed — so the gap is **prospective**, which is observation-class, which is why `finding` with no `pm:queue` is the right filing. ⛔ Grading is triage's channel; I am not queueing it as a rider just because the context is warm.

The platform-appended duplicate attribution footer is noted and correctly left alone.

## Next (mine)

Per-job gate conclusions, then flip ready → arm, in that order.

## ⚠️ My first landing check produced two false alarms, and both were mine

I scoped the negative-space greps with `awk` ranges anchored on the symbol names. Both came back **non-zero where I expected zero** — which, read literally, said the exemptions were still present *and* the write whitelist had grown, i.e. that this PR had done the one thing its fork condition forbade.

Both were wrong. The ranges started at the first *mention* (a doc comment near the top) and ran far past the intended block, sweeping in the test cases at `:777-832` that legitimately name all three tables. `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` is not defined in this file at all, so that range had no real end to find.

**Third time today a search construction nearly produced a false alarm on a correct merge** — after #7807's zero-that-wasn't and #8049's eight-that-didn't-matter. The first two were about trusting a count; this one is about trusting a **range**. Same remedy: locate the definition, then read the lines. Recorded in the seat post's notes.
